newsitem.title: FRANCE: GIAT ARMS MAKER (FN) SEES 1.3 BLN FFR NET LOSS.
newsitem.headline: GIAT ARMS MAKER (FN) SEES 1.3 BLN FFR NET LOSS.

text.p: French state-owned arms maker Giat Industries expects net loss of 1.3 billion francs ($252.5 million) after net 1995 loss of 10 billion, a company spokeswoman said on Friday.

The spokeswoman for Giat, which makes the Leclerc battle tank, said, "the net loss will be 1.3 billion francs," confirming a forecast given in an interview given by chairman Jacques Loppion to business daily Les Echos. He said losses would steepen in 1996 at its FN Belgian subsidiary.
Giat would need fresh funds at the start of next year as its working capital needs were rising with increased production of the Leclerc, Loppion said.
Giat is consuming large amounts of cash as its output of Leclercs has risen to 100-110 this year from 66 in 1995. It also has to fund a job lay-offs programme.

The company expects to make provisions of about 200 million francs for 1996 "which should have been accounted for in 1995," he said. Giat made 1995 provisions of 6.3 billion francs against expected losses.

Its next payment in February from the United Arab Emirates, for a $3.6 billion contract signed in 1993 for 436 Leclercs will be only five percent of the purchase price instead of the 20 percent it received earlier this year.
These elements coincided with French defence budget cuts and a spreading-out of payments by the government, he said.
"The authorities are currently considering how Giat will cross this difficult period," he said.

Giat needs to improve margins on the Leclerc to around 15 percent, which requires re-negotiating the French army's purchase price of its Leclercs. The current prices were based on 1991 costs, which were out of date, he said.
He did not say what the current margins were but Giat's current restructuring plan, which includes cutting 2,569 jobs out of a total 12,000, assumes the improved margin.
"Giat is absolutely not about to disappear," he said. The sale of Leclercs meant there would be a need for maintenance and modernisation for the next 30 years.
Losses at the Belgian FN small bore arms company would worsen in 1996 after turning negative in 1995, following many years of profits. The company would need a restructuring plan, he added.
Loppion said turnover for 1996 should rise to 6.3 billion francs from 1995's 5.4 billion.
Giat made operating loss of around 1.7 billion francs in 1995.
The spokeswoman said the 1996 net loss would be 1.3 billion.

This year Giat saved some 200 million francs in general overheads and cut 100 million in research and development spending. A rise in the dollar and improved controls over its financial operations have made a positive impact of 250 million.
But those gains would be offset by the 200 million francs of provisions, he told the newspaper.

Giat, hit by defence spending cuts and a bad call on dollar hedging on its Emirates sale, received a 3.7 billion franc state recapitalisation in March to offset accumulated losses of 5.2 billion francs up to the end of 1994.
Giat is trying to sell Leclercs to Saudi Arabia but is competing with the Desert Challenger made by British firm Vickers Plc and the Abrams M1A2 made by U.S. company General Dynamics Corp .
